title: प्रथमोनुवाकः
samhita: विज्य॒-न्धनुः॑ कप॒र्दिनो॒ विश॑ल्यो॒ बाण॑वाग्ं उ॒त । अने॑शन्न॒स्येष॑व आ॒भुर॑स्य निष॒ङ्गथिः॑ ॥
pada: विज्य॒मिति॒ वि = ज्य॒म्॒ । धनुः॑ । क॒प॒र्दिनः॑ । विश॑ल्य॒ इ॒ति॒ वि = श॒ल्य॒: । बाण॑वा॒निति॒ बाण॑ = वा॒न॒ । उ॒त । अने॑शन्न् । अ॒स्य॒ । इष॑वः । आ॒भुः । अ॒स्य॒ । नि॒ष॒ङ्ग॒थिः॑ ॥
krama: विज्य॒-न्धनुः॑ । धनुः॑ कप॒र्दिनः । क॒प॒र्दिनो॒ विश॑ल्यः । विश॑ल्यो॒ बाण॑वान् । बाण॑वाग्ं उ॒त । उ॒ताने॑शन् । अ॒ने॒शन्न॒स्य । अ॒स्येष॑वः । इष॑व आ॒भुः । आ॒भुर॑स्य । अ॒स्य नि॑ष॒ङ्गथिः । नि॒ष॒ङ्गथि॒रिति॑ निषङ्ग-इथिः ॥

sayana.text:
'Kapardi' is he who has a matted tuft of hair (kaparda). May the bow of that Rudra be 'vijyam', without a string. And also, let the 'banavan'—the quiver where the arrows stay—be 'vishalya'. May it be without projecting arrowheads, because of the shalyas (heads) of the arrows being hidden in its interior. May the arrows of this Rudra, hidden in the quiver, be 'aneshan'—unable to pierce.
...

22  

...let them be. May the 'nishangadhi'—the container of arrows—of this Rudra be 'abhu', scarcely capable. May it be capable only of holding the arrows by being hung on a peg, but not capable of having the arrows drawn out. Or, 'nishangadhi' means the sword-scabbard; may it also, as before, be capable only of holding the sword by being placed somewhere, but not capable of having the sword drawn out. (12)
sayana.sanskrit:
रुद्ररूपेण सहस्रसंख्याकान्यस्णिण यस्यासौ स तथा। शतसंख्या-
का इषुधयो वाणस्थापनकोशा यस्यासौ शतेषुघिस्ताद्यश हे रुद्र धनुरवतत्या-
वरोपितड्याकं कृत्वा शल्यानां वाणानां मुखा मुखानीपुगतलोहानामग्राणि
निशीर्येषुघिषु न्यग्भावेन शीर्णानि कृत्वा नोऽस्मान्मति सुमना अनुग्रहयुक्तः
सःशिवः शान्तो भव ॥ ११ ॥

भ० मा० भा० अथ द्वितीया । अवतत्येति। मुखेति तृतीयपादान्तः । हे सह-
स्राक्ष । व्याख्यातमृ। हे शतेषुघे। यस्य भूमिष्ठा इषवः सन्ति तस्य बहुभि-
रिपुधानैर्भिवतव्यमिति भावः। ' कर्मण्यधिकरणे च ' इति किमत्ययः। त्वं
धनुः पिनाकाख्यमवतत्यावततज्यं कृत्वा शल्यानां शराणां मुखा मुखानि
निशीर्यं नितरां विशीर्णानि कुण्ठीकृतानि कृत्वा नोऽस्माक्षुपिरे शिवः सुम-
नाश्च भव। सतामप्यपचाराणां क्षमया शिवः शान्तो भूत्वा मद्विषये मङ्गकौड-
यमिति सुमनस्केन च नित्यं त्वया भवितव्यमिति । यद्वेत्यमस्माभिः पार्-
थ्यंमानः सुमना एव भूत्वा भयहेतूनां धनुरादीनां चोपसंहाराद्पगतभयहेतुः
शिवो भवेति। ' सोमंनसी ' इत्युत्तरपदाचुदात्तत्वमृ॥ ११ ॥
॥ द्वादशीमृचमाह ॥
विज्यं धनुः कपर्दिनो विशल्यो बाणवाः उत ।
अनेशन्नस्येषंव आशुरस्य निषङ्गथिः ॥ १२ ॥

विज्यमिति वि–ज्यम् धनुः कपर्दिनः विशल्य इति वि–
शल्यः बाणवानिति बाण–वान् उत । अनेशन् अस्य इष्वः आशुः
अस्य निषङ्गगिथः ॥ १२ ॥

सा० भा० कपर्दी जटाजूटः सोऽस्यास्तीति कपर्दी रुद्रस्तस्य धनुर्विज्यं विग-
तज्याकमस्तु। उतापि च वाणा अर्धमिस्तिष्ठन्तीति वाणवानिषुधिः स च
विशल्योऽस्तु। इषुगतानां शल्यानां तदुदरे गोपितत्वेन विहरावित्रृतशल्यरहि-
तोऽस्तु। अस्य रुद्रस्येपवो वाणा इषुधौ मक्षिता अनेशन्वेद्धुमसमर्था


भवन्तु । अस्य रुद्रस्य निषङ्गथिर्वाणाधार आभुरस्तु ईषत्मभुरस्तु । कुञ्य-
निखातशङ्कावासञ्जितत्वेन वाणान्धारियतुमेव प्रभवतु । नतु वाणाकर्षणयोग्य
इत्यर्थः । अथवा निषङ्गतिः खद्गकोशः सोऽपि पूर्वेवत्कचिदारोपितत्वेन
खद्गं धारियतुमेव प्रभवतु नतु खद्गाकर्षणसमर्थः ॥ १२ ॥

म० भा० भा० अथ तृतीया । विञ्यमिति । कपर्दो जटाजूटस्तद्वतो देवस्य
धनुः पिनाकाख्यं विञ्यं विगतज्याकमास्तिवति शेषः । अथास्य देवस्य वाण-
षाणिषुधिर्वाणाः अस्मिन्सन्तीति सोऽपि विञ्ज्वयो विगतवाणोऽस्तु । पूर्वे
वाणवानपीदानों विञ्ज्वयो भूयादिति भावः । जताप्ययें । वाणवानपीत्यर्थः।
'दीर्घादिटि' इति रुत्वम् । आतोऽटीत्यनुस्वारः । किंचास्य देवस्य स्वभूता
इषवो नेञ्जन्दयाः स्युः । 'छन्दसि लुङ्लङ्' इति नञेराशिषि लुङ् ।
पुषादित्वाङ्लेरङ् नशिमन्योरलिञ्येत्वम् 'इत्येकारः । यद्वा—अस्येषुष्रेरिपवोऽ-
नेञ्जन्पत्र कापीषुधेरन्यत्राद्दरवास्तिष्ठन्तु । तेनायं विञ्ज्वयः संपद्यत इति
प्रकृतस्य समर्थनम् । किंचास्य देवस्य निषङ्गतिरय्यामुरस्तु । नितरां नियमेन
वा कोशेन सञ्जत इति निषङ्गः खद्गः स निधीयते यत्र स निषङ्गथिः
खद्गकोशः । परोक्षवचया धकारस्य थकारः । '' परोक्षप्रिया इव हि देवाः ''
इति । पूर्वेवत्किमत्ययः । आ ईषद्वतील्याहुः । आ ईषदर्थे । विपसंभ्य
इति ड्रुमत्ययः । व्यत्ययेनाऽऽऽडयपि भवति । किंचिन्न्यूनं भवनमाभवनं तच्च
खद्गेन विना सत्तामात्रेणावस्थानं निषङ्गधारणस्वभावस्य खद्गकोशस्य
निषङ्गेण सहावस्थानं पुष्कलभावस्तेन विनाऽवस्थानमाभवनमिति । तेन
सोऽपि खद्गग्रहितो वर्तेतामिति भावः । यद्वा निषञ्जते कोश इति निषङ्गथिः
खद्गः । 'नौ षड्धेधितन्' इति धथिन्मत्ययः । आभुरस्तु न्यूनशक्तिरस्तु
कुण्ठितप्रभावमीषञ्ज्वनमिति ॥

आसां तिसृणाशृचां पुरश्चरणम्—कृच्छं चरित्वाऽऽत्मानं संशोध्य नव
दिनानि जपेत्सिद्धो भवति । एताभिर्युंद्काले भूपतेरायुषान्यभिमन्त्र्य कुशक-
'टकानां सहस्रं जुहुयात् । युद्धोपनीताः शत्रवो हीयन्ते । ध्यानम्—

'' उदयद्भास्करकोटिमकाञ्जमादीप्तदहनपूर्णोनम् ।
भीषणमुजंगभूषं ध्यायेद्विविषायुधं रुद्रम् '' इति ।
द्वितीयस्य ध्यानम्—
'' रुद्रं सुरनियन्तारं शूलखद्वाङ्घारिणम् ।
ज्वालामाकाहृतं ध्यायेन्रक्तानामभप्रमदम् '' इति ॥ १२ ॥


॥ त्रयोदशीमृचमाह ॥
या ते हेतिर्मीढुष्टम हस्ते बभूव ते धनुः ।
तयाऽस्मान्विश्वतस्त्वर्मयक्ष्मया परिभुज ॥ १३ ॥
या ते हेतिः मीढुष्टमेति मीढुः—तम हस्ते बभूव ते धनुः ।
तयाँ अस्मान् विश्वतः त्वमृ अयक्ष्मया परीतिं भुज ॥ १३ ॥
सा० मा० हे मीढुष्टमातिशयेन कामाभिवर्षक या ते हेतिस्तव संबन्धि
खड्गादिरूपं यदायुधं यदपि ते तव हस्ते धनुर्वसुव । अयक्ष्मयाऽनुपद्रवका-
रिण्या तया हेल्या तथाविषेण धनुषा च त्वपस्मान्विश्वतः परिञ्भुज सर्वतः
परिपाळय ॥ १३ ॥

bhatta_bhaskara.dhyana: Meditation on Shiva as detailed in standard commentaries.
bhatta_bhaskara.text:
Now the third. 'Vijyam'. 'Kaparda' is the matted hair; the bow of the God who possesses that, named Pinaka, is 'vijyam'—let it be without a string (this is the understood remainder). Now, let the 'banavan'—the quiver in which the arrows are kept—be 'vishalya', without arrows. The idea is: may that which was formerly 'banavan' (possessing arrows) now be 'vijvayah' (without arrows). 'Uta' is used in the sense of 'also'. And also, may the arrows belonging to this God be 'aneshan'—may they not strike. The past tense is used in the sense of a prayer in the Veda. Or: may his arrows remain hidden elsewhere than in the quiver. By that, the preceding statement 'vijvayah' is supported. Furthermore, let the 'nishangadhi' of this God be 'abhu'. 'Nishanga' is the sword, which is bound or kept with a scabbard (kosha); that in which it is placed is the 'nishangadhi'—the scabbard. The 'dh' of 'dhi' is changed to 'th' in the Vedic style, for "the gods love the cryptic." 'A-bhu' means 'diminished' or 'empty'. 'A' is in the sense of 'little'. The scabbard's nature is to hold the sword; its being without the sword is its 'a-bhavanam' (non-being/emptiness). The idea is: let it also be without the sword. Or: 'nishangathi' means the sword itself. May it be 'abhu', of diminished power, its influence blunted.

For these three verses (10, 11, 12), the Purashcharana is: having performed Krichhra, purified oneself, and chanting for nine days, one achieves siddhi. With these, during war, after consecrating the king's weapons, one should offer a thousand oblations of Kusha grass. The enemies brought to the battle will be defeated.

Meditation (Dhyanam) [for Mantra 11]:
"One should meditate on Rudra, who is like crores of rising suns, with eyes full of blazing fire, adorned with terrifying serpents, and holding various weapons."
Meditation for the second [Mantra 12]:
"One should meditate on Rudra, the controller of the gods, holding the trident (shula) and the skull-staff (khatvanga), surrounded by a garland of flames, the destroyer of the pride of the enemies." (12)
...
bhatta_bhaskara.sanskrit:
अथ या ते हेतिरित्याद्यास्तिस्रोऽनुष्टुभः । ऋषिर्देवता च भग-
वानेव । हे मीढुष्टम । मीढ्वान्व्याख्यातः । अतिशयेन सेक्ता । या ते तव स्व-
यूता हेतिरायुधं धनुर्नाम तव हस्ते बभूव भवति । छान्दसो लिट् । ऊतियूती-
त्यादिना हिंसाकर्मणो हन्तेः किन्न उदात्तत्वमेतवं च निपात्यते । तया हेल्या
धनुर्नाम्या । अयक्ष्मया भक्तान्मल्यरोगहेतुभूतया । 'नञ्सुभ्याम्' इत्युत्तरपदा-
न्तोदात्तत्वमृ । विश्वतो भयहेतोरस्मांस्त्वं परिञ्भुज सर्वतः परिपाळय। सर्वका-
लं सर्वेण च मकारेण सर्वेस्माहुरितादस्मान्रक्ष । सांहितिको वकारोपजनश्छा-
न्दसः । उक्तं च षातिशास्त्रये 'उपसगैपाथ एपः' इत्यादि । भुजेर्विकरणव्य-
त्ययेन शः । यद्वा विश्वतो विश्वान्सपुत्रपौत्रानस्मान्पाहीति । सार्वेविभक्ति-
कस्तिसः । केचिदाहुः—हेतिर्हिंसा या ते त्वत्कर्तृका हिंसा । यदर्थे तव हस्ते
हिंसार्थेसाधनं धनुस्तिष्ठति तयाऽस्मानित्यादि तुल्यमृ ॥ १३ ॥

abhinava_shankara.dhyana: Meditation on Lord Maheshvara with resplendent Goddess.
abhinava_shankara.text:
"Let the bow of the matted-haired one (Kapardin) be unstrung, and the quiver too be emptied of arrows. Let the arrows of his become incapable of wounding, and let his quiver be swift [but empty]."

Now, even for the arrows that have been blunted, the prayer is offered for their incapacitation: "Vijyam iti" — may the bow of Kapardin (the Lord with matted hair, who is the Supreme Lord), be vijya — without its bowstring; and may the arrow-holder (bāṇavān — one who bears arrows) also be viśalya — devoid of arrows. Even if the quiver holds shafts, there is the concern about arrows elsewhere, hence the [mantra] says: "Aneśan iti" — may the arrows of this Kapardin be incapable of wounding, having attained destruction in the form of inability to pierce (aneśan — may they fail to reach; nāśa in the optative-like usage of the Vedic [aorist]). Furthermore, may his niṣaṅghiḥ (the quiver) be āśu (swift/ready) — meaning capable only of holding the quiver but not qualified to perform the task of pulling out and discharging the arrows. Here, [the text] "Prabhuśca dhanvana" and so forth constitutes a single mantra for the teacher. The seer (ṛṣi) of this pair of [mantras] is Nārada, the metre is Anuṣṭup, and the deity is Śrī Rudra. [The dhyāna-śloka is:] "One should meditate upon Rudra, blazing like ten million rising suns, his form like a flaming fire, his limbs adorned with fearsome serpents, bearing various weapons." Through this [mantra] enemies are destroyed. Thus [ends] the twelfth [mantra].

meanings.english: Bowstring; string of the bow; that which overpowers
meanings.nirukta: √jyā — 'jyāyate balam dadāti' (that which gives force/power). The bowstring is what propels the arrow — it is the source of the bow's destructive power. Also connected to 'jyāyas' (superior/overpowering).
meanings.vedantic: Releasing the bowstring (jyā) renders the bow inoperative. In Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad terms, if the bow (Oṃkāra) is for launching the arrow (jīva) at Brahman, then releasing the string suggests the cessation of the outward-projecting force — the return to stillness.

panini: P 7.1.18 — ā-stem feminine: acc. sg. ज्याम्

lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 2.8.85 — ज्या listed as bowstring: 'jyā guṇaḥ' — jyā and guṇa are synonyms for bowstring (notable: guṇa = quality/string — a rich double meaning).

meanings.nirukta: Yāska connects dhanvan to √dhan (to produce sound) — the bow is characterized by its resonant twang when released. Also related to √dhanv (to curve/run) — its arc shape. Nirukta 9.11 notes the relationship between the bow's curve and the concept of all-pervading reach.
meanings.vedantic: Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (2.2.4): 'dhanur gṛhītvā aupaniṣadaṃ mahāstram' — 'Taking up the great weapon, the bow of the Upaniṣads' — the bow is Oṃkāra (Praṇava). It is both the vehicle of destruction and liberation. In Śrī Rudram context, saluting the bow acknowledges the instrument through which divine will operates.

panini: √धन् + वनिप् (Uṇādi 4.113) → धन्वन् — vanip-pratyaya forms the n-stem noun
P 7.1.75 — an-anta (n-stem) declension paradigm: nom. धनुः (with P 8.2.7 n → anusvāra → ḥ), dat. धन्वने
P 6.4.8 — sarvanāmasthāna rules for the alternation between dhanvan-/dhanus- stems
P 8.2.7 — conversion of final n to visarjanīya in nom. sg.: dhanvans → dhanuḥ

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 2.20 — listed among āyudha-nāmāni (weapon names). The Naighaṇṭuka tradition pairs it with iṣu as the primary weapon-set.
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 2.8.85 (Kṣatriya-varga, Āyudha) — 'dhanuḥ koḍaṇḍam' — dhanus and koḍaṇḍa are synonyms for bow. Also 'cāpaḥ śarāsanam' as further synonyms.

meanings.english: The matted-haired one; one who wears braided locks; the one with twisted locks (like a cowrie shell)
meanings.nirukta: From kaparda — 'kapardaḥ keśa-bandhaḥ' (bound/twisted hair). 'Kapardo'sya asti iti kapardī' — one who possesses kaparda. The matted/twisted locks are a signature characteristic of Rudra-Śiva, representing asceticism (tapas).
meanings.vedantic: The matted hair (jaṭā) of Rudra symbolizes tapas (austerity) and the containment of cosmic energy. Śiva as kapardin is the supreme ascetic whose very hair holds the Gaṅgā (divine knowledge). In mantra 12: 'vijyaṃ dhanuḥ kapardinaḥ' — 'stringless be the bow of the matted-haired one'.

panini: P 5.2.109 — ini-pratyaya (possessive): kaparda + in → kapardin (possessing kaparda)

lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 1.1.29 — कपर्दी / कपालमाली listed among Śiva's epithets. Kaparda also means cowrie shell — Amarakośa 2.10.30.

meanings.english: Without arrowheads; freed from barbs; pointless (rendered harmless); with arrows extracted
meanings.nirukta: Vi (privative) + śalya (arrowhead). The arrows are described as having their barbs removed — rendered completely harmless. 'Vigatāni śalyāni yasya saḥ' — one whose arrows have lost their points.
meanings.vedantic: In mantra 12: 'viśalyo bāṇavān' — 'may his arrows be without points'. The prayer doesn't ask for the arrows to disappear — they remain, but are harmless. This is the Vedāntic insight that the world (jagat) need not be destroyed, only its harmful aspect removed.

panini: P 2.2.6 — vi-prefix in privative sense: vi + śalya → viśalya (without śalya)

meanings.nirukta: From √baṇ — 'baṇati śabdam karoti' (that which makes a sound) — the whistling arrow. Or from vaṇa (reed) — arrows were traditionally made from reeds.
meanings.vedantic: In mantra 12: 'viśalyo bāṇavān' — Rudra still possesses (vān) arrows (bāṇa) but they are without points (viśalya). The prayer preserves Rudra's identity as warrior while neutralizing the threat.

panini: P 5.2.94 — matup-pratyaya: bāṇa + vat → bāṇavat, nom. bāṇavān (possessing arrows)

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 2.20 — listed among āyudha-nāmāni alongside iṣu and śara.
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 2.8.86 — बाणः listed as arrow-synonym: 'iṣuḥ śaraḥ bāṇaḥ'.

meanings.english: And; also; moreover; as well as; further
meanings.nirukta: Vedic indeclinable conjunction (avyaya) expressing conjunction, addition, or emphasis. 'Uta' = 'api ca' (and also).
meanings.vedantic: Connects various divine aspects and attributes, showing that all manifest forms are manifestations of the one Supreme Lord.

meanings.english: They became powerless; they lost their ability; they became harmless; they could not reach [us]
meanings.nirukta: Negated verb: a + √īś (to be powerful/able). 'Aneśan' = 'they became unable/powerless'. Sāyaṇa: 'na prabhavanti' (they do not have power). Applied to Rudra's arrows — they became incapable of harm.
meanings.vedantic: In mantra 12: 'aneśan asya iṣavaḥ' — 'his arrows became powerless'. The prayer envisions a state where Rudra's weapons retain their form but lose their capacity to harm — transformation without destruction.

panini: P 3.3.175 — negated verbal form: a + neś/nīś + an

meanings.english: This; this here; this very (proximate demonstrative pointing to something nearby)
meanings.nirukta: Idam points to what is immediate and present, contrasted with adas (remote). In mantra 7: 'imāṃ rudrāḥ' — 'these Rudras here [in all directions]'.
meanings.vedantic: The proximate 'idam' (this) vs remote 'adas' (that) establishes a spatial theology — Rudra is both 'asau' (that one yonder — the transcendent sun) and manifest 'here' (imāṃ — in all directions through the Rudras). This is the saguṇa-nirguṇa polarity.

panini: P 7.2.108-109 — special suppletion forms: idam → imam/imām

meanings.english: Around; fully; completely; on all sides; away from
meanings.nirukta: Nirukta 1.3 — pari adds the sense of 'surrounding, encompassing, going around'. In mantra 15: 'pari te dhanvano hetiḥ asmān vṛṇaktu viśvataḥ' — 'may the weapon of your bow go around us [miss us] from all sides'.
meanings.vedantic: Pari (around/away) in the protective context means 'let the weapon go around us, avoiding us'. The prayer creates a shield of divine grace that the weapon itself respects.

panini: P 1.4.58 — pari classified as an upasarga
P 1.4.59 — modifies verbal meaning to add 'around/completely'

meanings.english: To become; to be; to arise; to exist; to happen
meanings.nirukta: Nirukta 2.1 — Yāska establishes √bhū as the root of all becoming. 'Bhavati' denotes coming-into-being, while 'babhūva' (perfect) indicates accomplished/established existence. The Nirukta treats bhū as the most productive root in the language.
meanings.vedantic: In Vedānta, √bhū represents the principle of manifestation — Brahman becoming the world. 'Babhūva te dhanuḥ' — 'your bow has become [auspicious]' — represents the transformation of the terrible into the benign through prayer.

panini: P 3.2.115 — liṭ lakāra (perfect): भू → ब + भू + व → बभूव (with reduplication per P 6.1.8)
P 3.4.87 — loṭ lakāra (imperative): भू + हि → भव (with guṇa per P 7.3.84)
P 3.2.107 — past participle: भू + क्त → भूत
P 3.3.18 — verbal noun formation: भू + क्तिन् → भूतिः (prosperity)

lexicographical_references.nighantu: Nighantu 1.1 — √bhū listed among the most fundamental sattā-vācaka dhātus (existence-denoting roots).
lexicographical_references.amara_kosha: Amarakośa 3.3.213 — भूतम् (past participle) listed meaning 'prāpta' (obtained) and 'jāta' (born). भूतानि as 'beings' appears in Amarakośa 1.1.7.

meanings.english: The quiver attached / tied onto the back
meanings.nirukta: From ni + sañj (niṣaṅga) + ithac pratyaya → niṣaṅgathiḥ (quiver for carrying arrows on the back).
meanings.vedantic: Refers to Rudras quiver remaining in its place without being drawn, symbolizing peace.
